meta.title: OAuth 2.0 authorization code + PKCE
meta.summary: How PKCE protects the authorization code for public clients.

steps.title: Create verifier + challenge
steps.narration: The app generates a random `code_verifier` and sends only its hash, the `code_challenge`, with the authorization request.

steps.title: Authorize
steps.narration: The user is redirected to the authorization server, signs in and consents. The server stores the challenge.

steps.title: Receive code
steps.narration: The server redirects back with a short-lived **authorization code**. On its own the code is not enough to get tokens.

steps.title: Exchange code + verifier
steps.narration: The app proves it started the flow by sending the original `code_verifier`. The server hashes it and compares it to the stored challenge.

steps.title: Call the API
steps.narration: With the access token the app calls the resource API on the user's behalf.

scenarios.title: What if the code is stolen?

steps.title: Attacker has the code
steps.narration: Suppose a malicious app on the device intercepted the redirect and holds the authorization code.

actions.text: Has the code, not the verifier

steps.title: Exchange rejected
steps.narration: The attacker cannot produce the `code_verifier`, which never left the real app. The hash check fails and no token is issued.
